commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[loom] Announce Slack actions before waits (#8839)

Require Marin Slack sessions to announce actions such as opening a pull
request or issue, or starting a run or deployment, in the source thread
before entering a wait or long-running monitor. Announcements include
the action identifier and link when available, and Loom status updates
do not replace the thread message.

This keeps the requester informed when a session begins CI or review
monitoring immediately after creating a pull request.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[grafana] Refine evaluation regression alerts (#8835)

Trigger `eval_regressed` when the latest Paloma macro loss, observed
within 30 minutes, exceeds the value from two evaluations earlier or
rises more than 2% from the preceding evaluation. Both comparisons use
samples with the same `execution_uid` and retain the latest three
samples from the existing 24-hour bounded query.

This removes alerts for an isolated increase of 2% or less when the new
value remains below the value from two evaluations earlier. The Grafana
test suite passes 262 tests.

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[cleanup] Delete unused eval and optimizer code, drop a shuffle copy (#8831)

Four independent cleanups.

zephyr's `ScatterWriter._flush` handed the output sink `buf.getvalue()`,
which
copies the whole compressed Parquet chunk before fsspec copies it again
into its
own write buffer. `buf.getbuffer()` passes a view instead, removing one
full copy
of every scatter chunk from the peak RSS that `zephyr/memory_budget.py`
sizes the
flush threshold against; chunks routinely run to hundreds of megabytes.

`run_save_logprobs_on_pod` and `run_trace_labeled_eval_on_pod` were the
last
users of the `*_on_pod` fray submission pattern that the lazy
ArtifactStep
migration (#6649) replaced with `remote(fn, resources=...)`, and nothing
has
called them since. Deleting them also removes their wrapper configs, the
HF hub
timeout constants, and the `job_failure_max_retries` field whose
validation
suggested it still controlled retries. Neither evaluation module imports
fray any
more.

levanter accepted five configuration knobs that no implementation reads,
so
setting any of them silently did nothing: `nesterov` on
`scale_by_adopt`,
`lax_map_scanned_layers` and `lax_map_batch_size` on `scale_by_soap`
(copied from
kron, which does use them), and
`Gpt2HyenaConfig.gradient_checkpointing_block_size`.
`HessianOptConfig` goes with them: an abstract `OptimizerConfig` holding
one more
ignored knob, with no subclass since Sophia was deleted in #2290.

iris spelled the archivable-file-type rule for task-output capture
(`S_ISDIR or S_ISREG or S_ISLNK`) four times across the inventory pass,
the tar
writer, and the empty-archive check, so changing which types are
archived meant
editing four places or letting the passes disagree about which entries
are
skipped. They now share `_is_archivable`. The inventory's if/else
collapsed with
it: both arms appended the same entry, and the byte accounting the
else-arm
guarded is a no-op for non-regular files, whose recorded size is already
zero.

---------

Co-authored-by: nightshift <nightshift@marin.local>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[codehealth] Persist review feedback for lint refinement (#8747)

Persist a weekly 30-day view of GitHub review state and lint telemetry
in the existing `context` PostgreSQL database. Hydration batches commit
with their sync checkpoints, edited pull requests and review events
retain version history, and a failed window resumes for at most three
attempts before abandonment. Exploration fails closed unless the newest
sync completed. The collector reconciles every paginated connection,
detects mutation during collection, and enforces GraphQL and REST
budgets.

Later syncs perform the bounded activity scan, edited-comment seed
queries, fingerprint rechecks, and Finelog query. Repository-wide
comment seeds are compared with compact fingerprints of the stored event
identity, body, and update timestamp. A matching event can reuse its
stored pull request after the pull-request fingerprint passes both scan
observations. New or edited events and changed pull requests still
trigger hydration. Hydrated PRs, child records, telemetry rows, and
reuse checkpoints use bounded multi-row database writes.

A production cold sync scanned 750 candidates and persisted 364
review-active PRs, 440 lint invocations, and 3,757 findings in 63.1
minutes. The original warm policy reused 164 of 364 PRs and took 46.6
minutes because every in-window seed forced hydration. The corrected
production run reused 350 of 357 relevant PRs, hydrated seven, and
completed in 247 seconds. GraphQL points fell from 355 to 206 and REST
requests from 249 to 56 relative to the original warm run. The [cache
smoke
report](https://loom.oa.dev/s/1xthg02m/artifacts/codehealth-cache-smoke)
records the exact windows and denominators.

The weekly Loom agent receives bounded commands for pull requests,
comments, source context, catalog rules, production rule activity, sync
status, and code-only rule probes. Probes hide the human comment and
record their context, rule, catalog, model, effort, output, and timing
identities. The agent edits normal rule YAML and opens a regular pull
request from a template when evidence supports a change. Its Markdown
report is a versioned Loom artifact with a typed channel result; no
fixed report renderer or corpus archive constrains the investigation.

The 63 lint rules move from lane Markdown files to ordered,
independently editable YAML while preserving production prompt text. The
[accepted
design](https://loom.oa.dev/s/1xthg02m/artifacts/codehealth-refinement-data-design)
records the storage and tool boundaries, and [Claude Fable's completion
review](https://loom.oa.dev/s/1xthg02m/artifacts/pr-8747-completion-review)
covers the implementation. The [production E2E
report](https://loom.oa.dev/s/1xthg02m/artifacts/codehealth-refinement-report)
analyzes 1,002 substantive human-review bodies across 219 PRs.

The unchanged 81-case catalog benchmark scored 81/81. A provisional
20-case live-context set scored 1/17 positive recall and 3/3 negative
specificity. Several provisional positives mapped a human concern to the
nearest rule even though the exact current rule should not fire; other
misses exposed limits in the local source-window prompt. Three new rules
have evidence across at least three PRs: consumer policy in shared
layers, duplicate config authority, and redundant exception wrappers. No
rule has enough representative current-catalog exposure for retirement.

The first live probe attempt also found a model-output boundary defect:
Luna returned negative decisions with explanatory fields that the schema
allowed and validation rejected. Negative results now canonicalize to
null confidence and finding while preserving raw output; all 16 failed
attempts completed under versioned retry keys. The incident record is
[Echo #302](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/302).

The branch passes 1,582 safe tests with 3 skipped and 5 expected
failures. The 40-test codehealth suite and targeted Pyrefly checks pass.
Production migration `m0014` is applied, three complete sync windows and
36 probe-attempt rows are stored, and the reports and typed result are
published. Slack delivery still needs an explicit `marin-eng` Loom
binding; the versioned artifacts and durable result do not depend on
that route.

Part of #8738

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Raise hero EP64 throughput (#8753)

Three changes increase Grug hero training throughput at EP64 without
changing the model function.

- The layer carry moves to pinned host under a new `offload_carry` remat
mode, and the latency-hiding scheduler turns on only in that mode.
Against the no-offload arm, this gives +0.44 MFU and lowers peak HBM
from 137.95 to 116.50 GiB.
- The QuACK gate/up interleave packs each gate/up pair of 16-bit values
into one `uint32`. The equivalent XLA stack-and-reshape reaches
approximately 1.9 TB/s; the packed elementwise form reaches 7.13 TB/s.
Against the stack-and-reshape arm, this gives +0.22 MFU. It carries a
hand-written VJP because `bitcast_convert_type` has no AD rule.
- The FA4 forward tile becomes 128x64 at the hero shape with
`d_model=6144`. Against the 64x64 forward tile, this gives +0.28 MFU.
Only the hero EP recipe selects it through
`attention_implementation=gpu_fa4_cute_wide`. The backward tile stays
64x64. The wide implementation requires SM100 with head dimension 128
and raises an error for other configurations.

Evidence comes from one GB200 NVL72 rack at EP64. Each one-change
ablation restores the production hero checkpoint. The score is the
median of `throughput/mfu` over restore steps +5 to +19.

The offload has one known hazard. When the offload, scheduler, and a
collective overlap limit above 1 are all enabled, the reloaded residual
races its backward consumer and corrupts training. No pair of the three
does (#8317). To prevent an inherited
`--xla_gpu_experimental_parallel_collective_overlap_limit` from
bypassing the safe setting, offload replaces any supplied value with 1.

This branch is based on #8684 for the required checkpoint-restore work.
Part of #8317.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[grafana] Treat nonterminal nightly statuses as running (#8825)

Treat every reported GitHub workflow status other than `completed` as an
active nightly. GitHub can report `requested`, `waiting`, and `pending`
in addition to `queued` and `in_progress`; those states otherwise appear
as failures.

Rows without a lifecycle status keep the prior health-based fallback.
This is a follow-up to #8812.

Co-authored-by: yoblin <268258002+yoblin@users.noreply.github.com>

[grafana] Show active nightlies as running (#8812)

Show queued and in-progress GitHub Actions runs as Running before
completed-run and quality-gate logic. Carry lifecycle status through the
backend projection, Grafana target N, and panel data parsing. The daily
header now reports categorical counts, and the cells, tooltips, and
legend name every operator state.

Validation passed: `uv run --with pytest --with pytest-timeout --with

advisory lint (no findings). `uv run --no-project infra/ci/run_tests.py`
completed successfully but selected no packages for these Grafana paths.
